events.title: Cristiano Ronaldo announces retirement from international football
events.summary: The announcement by the footballing legend comes just weeks after a public spat with Portugal coach Jorge Jesus over playing time.

events.title: Bomb threats disrupt several flights across Europe
events.summary: At least a dozen flights were either diverted or landed with a military escort after bomb or security threats. The first reported case involved a flight from Dublin to Rome landing outside Paris and more soon followed.

events.title: What the Democrats' midterms win means for the US economy and Trump
events.summary: From high oil prices and data centers to tariffs and mounting debt, economic concerns played a key role in the crushing defeat of President Donald Trump's Republicans. So can the Democrats now make a difference?

events.title: 36 years later: Hungary opens Communist-era secret service files
events.summary: Decades after the end of Soviet rule, Hungary is releasing all its secret service files. The disclosure is sparking fresh debate about informants, guilt and responsibility.

events.title: The 2011 discovery of neo-Nazi killers aired biases in German policing
events.summary: Many questions still surround the National Socialist Underground whose existence was revealed by neo-Nazi terrorist Beate Zschäpe on November 4, 2011. How has German society reacted to NSU crimes? Has justice been done?

events.summary: Despite reporting her husband to the police and pleading for protection, Arlinda Zekaj was brutally murdered. Now, thousands in Kosovo are protesting what they say is a dramatic failure of state institutions.

events.title: Gold for the West Bank: Meet Palestinian karate champ Mariam Bsharat
events.summary: The occupied West Bank is not an obvious breeding ground for sporting success. But Mariam Bsharat, 17, has beaten the odds to become a karate world champion and is making a new life in Germany.

events.title: Harry Potter films turns 25 ahead of new TV series' release
events.summary: In 2001, "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone" hit cinemas and took the world by storm. Today, anticipation for the new series is high, but its creator, J.K. Rowling, remains a controversial figure.

events.title: Leading ice hockey nations, sponsors oppose Russia's return
events.summary: Ice hockey's governing body says the impact of a court decision forcing it to reinstate Russia presents "significant practical and sporting challenges." Several leading nations say they won't play against Russian teams.

events.title: BMW reports lower Q3 earnings as China woes mount
events.summary: BMW reports a drop in profits in the July to September quarter amid fierce competition from China.

events.title: Germany's celebrated children's author Janosch has died
events.summary: Bear, Tiger and Tiger-Duck: The author and illustrator Janosch achieved world fame with his heartwarming children's figures. He died at the age of 95.

events.summary: Some studies have linked disgust sensitivity to socially conservative attitudes. But does disgust shape our politics, or do our beliefs shape what we find disgusting?

events.title: How Berlin's Arab queers are building their community
events.summary: As the co-founder of the ADIRA Drag Festival, Lebanese performance artist, drag performer, DJ and cultural organizer Hassandra has become an essential part of Berlin's queer artistic landscape.

events.summary: The Republic of Cyprus long balanced ties between Russia and the West. Now, it is phasing out Russian weapons, expanding defense cooperation with the United States and redefining its place in the Eastern Mediterranean.

events.summary: The bomb threats involved two passenger planes bound for Warsaw, a Ryanair flight from London to Spain, two flights to Rome and a flight traveling from Israel to the Bulgarian capital, Sofia. No explosives were found.

events.summary: Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel has died following a collision with the opposing goalkeeper. The Spanish second-division club has said it is "heartbroken" by the loss.

events.title: Asian Cup postponed due to Middle East conflict
events.summary: The Asian Cup has become the latest sporting event to be affected by the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. Organizers cite "exceptional circumstances" in Saudi Arabia, which has seen several Houthi attacks of late.

events.title: Could the AI boom make borrowing more expensive in Europe?
events.summary: France, Germany and Italy face a volatile bond market as war inflation bites. With US tech giants now issuing billions in AI bonds, they are competing with cash-strapped European governments.

events.summary: A security conference in the German capital is addressing defending Europe against threats from Russia. Meanwhile, Germany's justice minister wants to raise penalties for sexual offenses. DW has more.

events.summary: What happens when your name evokes laughter or ridicule? Research points to negative life outcomes, but some people learn to embrace unfortunate names.

events.title: Teddy Riner candidacy 'illustrative of this hunger for an alternative' to Le Pen or Mélenchon
events.summary:
As Teddy Riner throws his hat in the race for the French presidency, amid France's sociopolitical and economic crises.
 
François Picard is pleased to welcome Lex Paulson, Director of Executive Programs at UM6P School of Collective Intelligence at at Mohammed VI Polytechnic University.
 
The prospect of Olympic judo champion Teddy Riner entering France's presidential race raises questions that extend well beyond the political ambitions of a celebrated athlete. At a time when traditional parties are struggling to mobilize voters and the political center remains deeply fragmented, Riner's emergence points to a broader transformation in democratic competition: the growing importance of personal credibility, public visibility and the capacity to embody an alternative to established political elites.
 
In an interview with France 24, Lex Paulson, Professor of Collective Intelligence at Mohammed VI Polytechnic University, argues that the changing relationship between voters and political institutions is reshaping the conditions under which political outsiders can emerge.
 
"The currency of politics now is no longer just money to buy television advertisements or open offices. It's the ability to capture attention."
 
For Paulson, Riner's celebrity status gives him a considerable advantage in an increasingly fragmented media environment. Yet visibility alone does not confer political credibility. While the Olympic champion's public commitments against racism and xenophobia may resonate with voters, Paulson questions whether he has articulated a sufficiently developed political vision to become a serious presidential contender.
 
The deeper issue, however, is not whether Riner can win. It is what his potential candidacy reveals about the weakness of France's traditional political alternatives and the growing demand for leaders whose personal histories, values and commitments resonate with citizens.
 
"Voters don't vote for policies. Voters vote for people they sense will stand up for them."
 
Paulson's analysis connects this demand for political identification to a wider crisis of democratic representation. Voters, he suggests, increasingly perceive professional politicians as a distant governing class that listens to citizens only during electoral campaigns.
 
"People don't feel like they're being listened to except for the few weeks before an election."
 
Seen in this light, Riner's emergence is less an isolated celebrity phenomenon than a symptom of the changing relationship between political authority, public trust and democratic participation. The central challenge facing France's next generation of leaders may therefore be not simply to develop compelling policies, but to restore citizens' sense that political institutions are responsive to their lives.
 
As Paulson concludes, the real political opportunity lies in reimagining governance itself: bringing decision-making closer to citizens and giving them a more meaningful voice in the democratic process.

events.title: Trump ally Jim Jordan elected House Republican leader after midterm defeat
events.summary: Jim Jordan, a hardline ally of President Donald Trump, was elected US House Republican leader on Tuesday, defeating Steve Scalise 106-73 in a secret ballot, US media reported. He replaces Mike Johnson after Republicans lost both chambers of Congress in last week’s midterm elections and will lead the party’s opposition.

events.title: US charges three 'Iranian operatives' over RAF Fairford terror plot
events.summary: The US Justice Department on Tuesday charged three men it described as Iranian operatives over an alleged September terrorist plot at Britain's RAF Fairford airbase in England. Prosecutors said one suspect directed individuals to drive vans, some carrying fuel barrels, to the base, which housed US military aircraft and personnel.

events.title: West Bank: Population and healthcare actors, such as MSF, 'still facing movement restrictions'
events.summary: Eve Irvine is pleased to welcome Frederica Venturi of Doctors Without Borders (MSF). The withdrawal of Israeli forces from Hebron has not brought an end to the humanitarian crisis. According to Venturi, some 3,300 Palestinians were forcibly displaced, 15 houses were reportedly demolished, and continuing restrictions on movement have obstructed access to essential healthcare. "Those families whose houses were demolished have nowhere to go back to." Venturi describes how the "movement restrictions during the lockdown prevented medical teams from reaching communities." Hospitals are also reporting shortages of essential medicines.

events.title: 'Europe not going anywhere': G7 summit a 'signal to Russians' that Europe is standing behind Ukraine
events.summary: As the US Midterms reshape Ukraine diplomacy, Annette Young is pleased to welcome James Townsend, Atlantic Council's Senior Advisor at the Scowcroft Center's for Transatlantic Security Initiative. "Europe is not going anywhere." With this unequivocal assessment, Townsend, taking place alongside trilateral negotiations in Abu Dhabi. While the latter may command international attention, Townsend argues that the Paris meeting carries a message of its own: European support for Ukraine is intended to remain durable, and Moscow should not mistake diplomatic negotiations for an erosion of Western resolve. The G7 meeting therefore emerges as more than a forum for diplomatic declarations. It represents a test of Western cohesion, the credibility of future military and financial assistance, and Washington's willingness to endorse a common position on Ukraine. As Townsend emphasizes, the final communiqué will also be "a test as far as what Marco Rubio is going to agree to put his name to."

events.title: Eisenkot pushes October 7 inquiry as Netanyahu targets Arab parties in tense new parliament
events.summary: Gadi Eisenkot, the politician tasked with forming a new Israeli government, pledged on Tuesday to launch an official inquiry into Hamas's October 7, 2023 attacks and reverse many of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's policies as the new parliament was sworn in a tense opening session that saw rival parties trade barbs over the possibility of forming a government with the support of Arab lists.

events.title: 'Central role in ecosystem: If something happens to Nvidia, it's going to be a catastrophe'
events.summary: Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Raphaëlle d’Ornano, Founder and Managing Partner of D’Ornano + Co. “Nvidia has an absolutely central role in the ecosystem,” she explains, “If something happens to Nvidia, it's going to be a catastrophe.” When the discussion turns to geopolitics, she warns, “there is a real war happening here. It's an economic war,” describing the competition for frontier AI capabilities as a struggle with profound economic, military, and societal implications. The resulting analysis reveals an industry characterized by extraordinary technological momentum, but increasingly shaped by concentrated corporate power, geopolitical confrontation, and political resistance to its physical infrastructure.

events.title: Anthropic eyes $1.4 trillion valuation in blockbuster IPO
events.summary: US firm Anthropic, the company behind the Claude AI chatbot, has announced it will offer 825 million shares at a price between $70 and $78 apiece during its planned IPO.  This will give the firm a valuation of around 1.4 trillion dollars. The blockbuster IPO will come at a time investors are becoming increasingly concerned about risks associated with the AI boom. But first, chip giant Nvidia continues to face pressure over its CEO's love affair with a suspected Chinese spy.

events.title: Asymmetric cyberwarfare: 'States increasingly use cyberattacks in support of their other objectives'
events.summary: Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Rafe Pilling, Director of Threat Intelligence in the Sophos Counter Threat Unit (CTU). How can a minor cyber intrusion disrupt food supplies, expose the weaknesses of industrial infrastructure and become an instrument of geopolitical confrontation? The cyberattacks targeting supermarket refrigeration systems in France offer a revealing illustration of how digital vulnerabilities can translate into tangible economic disruption and potentially broader threats to society. As Pilling explains, “With a small amount of effort from the adversary side, they can create a large impact, in this case destroying food and producing empty shelves or empty refrigeration units in stores.” This asymmetry lies at the heart of contemporary cyber conflict, in which modest technical interventions can produce disproportionate economic and operational consequences

events.title: US soldier arrested in Britain on suspicion of assisting Russian intelligence
events.summary: UK police arrested a senior member of the US Army on Tuesday on suspicion of assisting Russian intelligence, adding that the arrest was not related to other counter-terror investigations. The 41-year-old man was detained near the city of Gloucester, west England, and remains in custody.

events.title: What the hack? Europeans face growing psyops and cyberattacks
events.summary: So this time, it's Iran, not Russia? France - reportedly acting on US intelligence - summoning Tehran’s ambassador over last month’s hacking of hundreds of supermarket refrigerators that overheated, 15 of which even caught fire. Why now at a time when Iran’s trying to break its international isolation?

events.title: Filming amongst body bags: New Colombian president’s comms campaign sparks backlash
events.summary: Since taking office in August, new far-right Colombian president Abelardo de la Espriella has shared video after video promoting his security forces – especially operations they’ve carried out against armed groups. In some, De la Espriella speaks standing among body bags. Others feature prisoners or look like they were taken from an action film. However, there’s been growing outcry about his social media glorification of repressive policies.

events.title: French police search Ritz, glitzy Al Fayed properties in women-trafficking probe
events.summary: French police have searched several properties, including the Ritz hotel in Paris, in relation to an investigation into a suspected international network trafficking women for Mohamed Al Fayed, prosecutors told AFP on Tuesday. The Ritz is just one of the late tycoon's high-end ventures where victims have said they faced abuse.

Friedrich Merz, Federal Chancellor of Germany, said that Germany currently faces a historic test over antisemitism.

events.title: US Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth calls impeachment moves 'a farce'

events.title: Who exactly is Pete Hegseth, the Pentagon chief facing an impeachment bid?
events.summary: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth on Tuesday dismissed the impeachment effort against him as "a political spectacle". He made the comments a day after Republican Thomas Massie launched a bid to impeach him over his handling of the unpopular war in Iran and other actions. But who is Pete Hegseth? A former Fox News host and military veteran, he has become one of the most prominent figures in the Trump administration.

events.summary: France has been buffeted for months by street protests. They began in September ​with students ‌demanding the renovation of school buildings, more teachers and ⁠university reforms but then turned into broader cost-of-living protests, drawing in trade unions and political activists, and sometimes ‌turning violent.

He also hailed US-mediated talks between Russia and Ukraine in Abu Dhabi as "very productive" and said the discussions should be expanded to include Europeans at the table.

events.title: REPLAY: Pentagon chief Hegseth holds news briefing amid impeachment push

events.summary: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth dismissed a move to impeach him by a Republican lawmaker as a “farce” and a political “stunt” on Tuesday. events.summary: The University of Mississippi is investigating the incident after a video caught two women mimicking apes outside three Black students’ front door.

events.title: Nvidia hires former acting U.S. attorney to probe Jensen Huang affair
events.summary: Nvidia shares have tumbled by more than 10% since Monday, erasing almost $500 billion in market value.

events.title: Call her candid: Sofia Franklyn’s memoir details falling out with Alex Cooper
events.summary: “Daddy Issues” is a tell-all from Franklyn’s side about the end of her business relationship and friendship with Cooper, who went on to helm “Call Her Daddy” solo.

events.title: The Vikings may have acquired the only missing piece for their Super Bowl run
events.summary: After another week of uninspiring quarterback play, the Minnesota Vikings acquired Kirk Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders. He could be the missing piece in a Super Bowl run.

events.title: Thomas Markle, Meghan’s father, cut off his ankle monitor, DOJ says
events.summary: Markle, who was arrested on suspicion of keeping child sexual abuse material in storage units in California, was taken into custody shortly after he removed the monitor, officials said.

events.title: Central Park serial rape suspect arrested in Florida, NYPD says
events.summary: Police and U.S. marshals captured Dereck Rivera-Deleon at his job at a Burger King in Miami.

events.title: Senior U.S. Army soldier arrested in U.K. on suspicion of assisting Russian intelligence
events.summary: The 41-year-old man was arrested “as part of an investigation by Counter Terrorism Policing” near the ⁠city of Gloucester, ​in the west ⁠of England, British police said.

events.title: U.S. soldier charged with spying for Russia
events.summary: A U.S. soldier was arrested in the U.K. and charged with spying for Russian intelligence agencies. NBC News’ Kelly O’Donnell reports.

events.title: Russia and Ukraine hold nearly 4 hours of U.S.-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi
events.summary: Three-way talks between Russia, Ukraine, and the United States opened in the United Arab Emirates, as Washington renews its push to end the Ukraine-Russia war. NBC News' Matt Bodner breaks down the developments from the round of peace talks.

events.title: Russia's last major independent newspaper shuts down citing Kremlin assault on free press
events.summary: Novaya Gazeta, renowned for uncovering human rights abuses and corruption through fierce reporting, closes its doors after more than three decades. The news outlet says it's shutting down due to government pressure from the Kremlin. NBC News' Matt Bodner reports.

events.title: Russell Brand is sentenced to 10 years and six months for rape and sexual assault
events.summary: Actor Russell Brand has been sentenced to 10 years and six months in a British prison for rape and sexual assault. Brand's victims told the court that they are still living with daily trauma because of what happened to them. NBC News' Danny Cevallos explains how Brand's sentence was determined.

events.title: Nvidia opens investigation after CEO’s affair with alleged Chinese spy
events.summary: Huang acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife in an employee memo. The board said it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised.

events.title: Russell Brand sentenced to more than 10 years in prison for rape and sexual assaults
events.summary: The 51-year-old comedian and actor was found guilty in a British court last week.

events.title: Gunman with far-right views who killed 6 in Poland shooting rampage dies in hospital
events.summary: The man, described as being his mid-20s, was shot by police during Saturday’s attack in the main square of Poland’s second-largest city.

events.title: Parents, sister of far-right Kraków shooter found dead in family home
events.summary: Three bodies found in the home of the 24-year-old shooter in Saturday’s rampage in the heart of Kraków, Poland, belonged to the gunman’s family, police said.

events.title: Gunman kills 6 in ‘terror attack’ in Poland, officials say; 3 others found dead in his home
events.summary: A gunman described as having “ultranationalistic” beliefs fatally shot six people while driving through a public square Saturday in Krakow, Poland, officials said, in what the country’s defense minister characterized as a “terror attack.” Three of his relatives were later found dead in his home.

events.title: Pope Leo, who had cancer surgery weeks ago, begins South American tour
events.summary: Less than a month after Pope Leo XIV underwent cancer surgery, he set off on what the Vatican called a “homecoming” tour of South America.

events.title: Investors try to regain their footing after tech stocks tank
events.summary: Tech stocks in the U.S. steadied Friday after suffering one of their worst routs in years, as investors weighed the prospect of an AI investment slowdown.

events.title: Wave of bomb threats against European airliners triggers diversions and tarmac searches
events.summary: No explosives have been found, and it isn’t clear who or what is behind the calls, but the threats alone have caused chaos in the skies and airports.

events.title: Clashes erupt in France as ‘Black Thursday’ protests sweep the nation
events.summary: “Everything is going up except wages and pensions,” the country’s main unions said. “Anger is immense.”

events.title: Russell Brand found guilty of rape and sexual assault
events.summary: Six women alleged that the British comedian had sexually assaulted them at his home, in hotels and public bathrooms. Brand has denied all claims.

events.title: Melania Trump calls for ‘enduring’ Russia-Ukraine peace as she hosts top officials at the White House
events.summary: Ukraine has been reeling from the worst collapse in relations with Washington since the start of the war.

events.title: U.S. Marine dies in Japan during training, military says
events.summary: The person, who has yet to be named, died Tuesday in Okinawa, the 3rd Marine Division said.

events.title: U.S. will stop $4B in aid to Israel at the end of the year, Trump says
events.summary: Oil prices slid in response to the deal, which the president said was Netanyahu’s idea.

events.title: U.S. military carries out limited strikes on Iran’s Qeshm Island
events.summary: The strikes, which appeared to be limited as opposed to a full return to hostilities, came on the eve of crucial American midterm elections.

events.title: Supermarkets across Europe hit by new fridge cyberattacks
events.summary: The incidents caused temperature spikes and spoiled food at stores in Sweden, the Netherlands, Belgium, Ireland, Luxembourg and Estonia. It follows a similar cyberattack in France last month.

events.title: Fake alerts warn of nuclear danger as Ukraine and Russia report emergency app hacks
events.summary: The dueling accusations came just as a rare humanitarian ceasefire between the two sides ended, raising fears of intensified fighting.

events.title: Israel’s president says parties need to engage with ‘open heart’ to avoid fresh election
events.summary: “Creative solutions” are needed to prevent another round of elections, Isaac Herzog has stressed, after no faction emerged with an obvious path to power.

events.title: Minor detained after U.S. warned Russia of possible Moscow terrorist attack, FSB says
events.summary: The FSB said it “verified” the information received from U.S. law enforcement, and “as a result of these operations, a Russian minor was detained,” Russia’s Tass news agency reported.

events.title: Stores looted in German riots as Gen Z activists protest living costs, military service
events.summary: Police said Molotov cocktails were thrown at the emergency services, as protests grew in Germany following weeks of unrest in France.

events.title: Massive protests sweep Europe over cost of living and strained public services
events.summary: Massive protests were sweeping Europe on Saturday as part of demonstrations driven by the cost of living and deficient public services, with police bracing for potential violence after recent looting and riots.
